name: architecture
description: Structured architecture or design review from multiple engineering perspectives. Each reviewer focuses on different cross-cutting concerns.

arguments.name: design
arguments.description: Description of the architecture, system design, or technical approach

arguments.name: workloads
arguments.description: Key use cases, workloads, or scenarios the design must handle

arguments.name: priorities
arguments.description: Non-functional priorities (e.g., "latency, cost, simplicity, observability")

arguments.name: uncertainties
arguments.description: Areas where you feel most unsure or want extra scrutiny

name: assumptions
description: Surface and challenge hidden assumptions in a plan, design, or idea. Identifies implicit premises that could be risky if wrong.

arguments.name: plan
arguments.description: The plan, design, or idea to analyze for hidden assumptions

arguments.name: constraints
arguments.description: Known hard constraints that are definitely true

arguments.name: concerns
arguments.description: Areas where you feel uncertain or worried

name: blindspots
description: Hunt for missing considerations, overlooked risks, and gaps in a proposal. Acts as a panel of critical reviewers looking for what might be underweighted.

arguments.name: proposal
arguments.description: The plan, code, design, or proposal to review for blindspots

arguments.name: covered
arguments.description: What you think you have already addressed or considered

arguments.name: risk_tolerance
arguments.description: Your risk tolerance level: low, medium, or high

name: diverge_converge
description: Structure divergent thinking (explore many options) followed by convergence (evaluate and select). Maximizes creative exploration before narrowing down.

arguments.name: challenge
arguments.description: The problem or challenge to solve

arguments.name: width
arguments.description: Exploration width: "wild" for creative/unconventional, "focused" for practical

arguments.name: convergence_criteria
arguments.description: What makes a solution "good" - criteria for evaluating options

name: perspectives
description: Analyze a problem from multiple perspectives. Each LLM adopts a different analytical lens (e.g., security, performance, UX) for comprehensive multi-angle analysis.

arguments.name: problem
arguments.description: The problem, design, or code to analyze

arguments.name: perspectives
arguments.description: Comma-separated analytical lenses (e.g., "security, performance, UX, maintainability")

arguments.name: context
arguments.description: Additional background or constraints

name: red_team
description: Conduct attack surface analysis from multiple angles. Each reviewer focuses on different risk dimensions (security, privacy, abuse, compliance).

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: The system, feature, code, or plan to red-team

arguments.name: threat_model
arguments.description: Known threat actors, attack scenarios, or security context

arguments.name: dimensions
arguments.description: Risk dimensions to focus on (e.g., "security, privacy, abuse, compliance, reputation")

name: reframe
description: Reframe a problem from multiple angles and abstraction levels. Helps break out of mental ruts by viewing the problem differently.

arguments.name: problem
arguments.description: The current problem statement or challenge

arguments.name: stuck_on
arguments.description: What specifically you are stuck on or frustrated by

name: tradeoffs
description: Compare options with explicit criteria and trade-off analysis. Provides structured evaluation to help make informed decisions.

arguments.name: options
arguments.description: The options to compare (comma-separated list or detailed descriptions)

arguments.name: criteria
arguments.description: Evaluation criteria (comma-separated, e.g., "cost, complexity, performance")

arguments.name: context
arguments.description: Decision context, constraints, or background

arguments.name: weights
arguments.description: Which criteria matter most (priority order or weights)
